root_cause: EpochResolver calls onMembersChanged without awaiting it, and the onHistorySynced profile send ran as an untracked IIFE; neither was in pendingDrainRef, so teardownForReplace could destroy/rejoin a group while the members-changed body (persist/reload, then `void mlsGroup.commit()` with no re-check) or the profile send still ran on the old MarmotGroup.
fix: runTracked(pending, groupId, work) in replaceTeardown.ts tracks the work synchronously from its start; teardownForReplace ends with one more bounded wait for work added during its own waits (skipped after a timeout). The members-changed body moved to membersChangedSync.ts (syncOnMembersChanged): it awaits the auto-commit and gates it on mayCommit (same client and the group not in replacingRef), so a replace blocks it but an effect restart alone does not. MarmotContext runs it (with a warn on failure) and the profile send through runTracked.

tests_added.kinds: real runTracked + teardownForReplace: suspended work blocks a replace, never-settling work fails closed, rejections/sync throws release it, work started during the leftover or idle wait is waited for, another group's work does not block; one timeout per stuck piece (fake timers); each pending step holds back the next. syncOnMembersChanged: parity cases, no commit while being replaced, commit after an effect restart only, resolves after the commit. Source scan of the MarmotContext wiring.

mutation.survivors: equivalent: timesOut's 'done' placeholder (only compared with 'timeout'); the late wait's length guard/empty fallback (Promise.all([]) resolves at once)

e2e.result: non-relay 72 passed; relay 353 passed, 19 skipped, 0 failed; no INVALID marker.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The added late wait silently made the earlier per-step timeouts redundant for the outcome; only Stryker showed that step ORDER was then untested, which needed explicit 'a pending step holds back the next' tests.
retrospective.surprised_by: Reusing isCurrentGroup for the commit re-check would also drop the auto-commit on a plain effect restart (same MarmotGroup instance); the reviewer caught it, hence the narrower replacingRef-based gate.
